Friday. Simran opened the bank site and linked the instalment for the education loan to auto-debit, set to leave the account the day after salary arrives. Damini, who had missed a due date last year, watched over the shoulder.

Next Thursday. A text arrived: "Balance below the set limit." Simran had added that alert too. The salary was a day late and the alert gave time to move money across before the debit.

Two months later. Simran opened the passbook. Both instalments had gone on time. "Automation only works if I still look at the balance," Simran said. Damini set up the same thing that evening.

qa.q: When was the auto-debit set to leave the account?
qa.a: The auto-debit was set for the day after salary arrives.

qa.q: How did Simran feel when the low-balance alert arrived?
qa.a: Simran was probably relieved, because the alert came in time to move money across before the debit despite the late salary.

qa.q: What could Simran do if the salary is delayed again, and why?
qa.a: Simran could keep a small buffer in the account, because a late salary should not cause a missed debit.

qa.q: How might Damini see Simran's auto-debit after the missed date last year?
qa.a: Damini probably felt encouraged, since the plan solved a problem that had already caused trouble, and copied it that evening.

grounding: A graduate links the instalment to auto-debit a day after salary credit and sets a balance alert, since automation prevents forgetting but the balance still needs watching.

subtype: Approach: set up auto-debit with a reminder [Action]
passage:
Madhav, you forgot your EMI date again? Sit. When I was new here, fifteen years ago, Preeti from accounts forgot hers twice in three months. The bank charged me each time, and my father got a phone call.
So I did three things, in this order. First, I asked the bank to take the EMI automatically on the 2nd, one day after salary came in on the 1st. Second, I set a balance alert: if the account went below ₹5,000, my phone would tell me. Third, I stopped telling myself I'd remember.
It worked for two years. Then one month the salary came late, on the 3rd, and the auto-debit bounced. The alert had warned me on the 1st; I just ignored it. So automation helps, Madhav, but it doesn't think for you. Now go and set yours up before lunch.

qa.q: On what date did Preeti ask for the EMI to be taken?
qa.a: On the 2nd, one day after salary came in on the 1st.

qa.q: How might young Preeti have felt when the auto-debit bounced?
qa.a: Annoyed and a little embarrassed, since the balance alert had given a warning that was ignored.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Preeti's story, and what did it teach?
qa.a: The late salary that made the auto-debit bounce; it showed that automation helps but the balance alert still has to be heeded.

qa.q: How might Preeti's father have felt getting the bank's phone call?
qa.a: Probably worried and caught off guard, which may be part of why those missed EMIs stayed with Preeti.

grounding: Shows a borrower setting the EMI to auto-debit a day after salary with a balance alert, while learning the balance still needs watching.

subtype: Approach: set up auto-debit with a reminder [Action]
passage:
Suraj had two days before his company sent him to a hydro project in the hills of Kinnaur, where colleagues said the phone signal came and went for weeks. His first EMI was due on the 5th, and he would be up there.
So on Thursday, at the branch near the office, he did it step by step. He filled in the auto-debit form so the EMI would leave on the 2nd, a day after salary. He asked the clerk to switch on an SMS alert for any balance under ₹8,000. Then he wrote the EMI amount, ₹7,400, on a card for his wallet.
Raghav, travelling with him, shook his head. 'You'll forget the card exists.'
'That's fine. The bank won't forget.'
On the 3rd, in a tea shop with one bar of signal, his phone buzzed: EMI paid. On the 12th, another buzz: balance under ₹8,000. He'd been spending more on site than planned. He cut back on the canteen extras.

qa.q: What might Suraj have been worried about before leaving for Kinnaur?
qa.a: He was anxious that the weak signal would make him miss the EMI date, so he wanted the payment to happen without him.

qa.q: What else could Suraj do while the signal is patchy?
qa.a: Check his balance whenever he gets signal, and keep a bit more buffer in the account so the auto-debit never bounces.

qa.q: How does Raghav see Suraj's preparation?
qa.a: Raghav thinks the wallet card is pointless, but sees that the real safety is the bank handling it automatically.

grounding: Shows a graduate linking the EMI to auto-debit a day after salary and setting a low-balance alert, which still needs watching.
